lines.t: Nintendo refused to sell this game. Fifteen years later, it just broke its own record.
The Binding of Isaac came out in September 2011. Two people made it in about three months, using Flash.
You play a crying kid named Isaac, escaping into a basement full of monsters. Your weapon is your own tears.
Every run is random. New rooms, new items, new bosses. Die once, and you start over.
The dungeons were inspired by the very first Legend of Zelda.
The story comes from the Bible, and that scared Nintendo. In 2012 they blocked it from the 3DS, over questionable religious content.
Its creator expected to sell a few hundred copies. It sold a million in about a year, and five million by 2015.
YouTubers made it famous, with endless Let's Play videos.
Funny detail: in 2011 it was up for best indie game, and lost to Minecraft.
The remake, Rebirth, hid a secret character behind a puzzle meant to last. Players data-mined it in 109 hours.
And it never stopped growing: Rebirth in 2014, Repentance in 2021, and online co-op in 2024, which is set to hit consoles this November.
Then this June, a 90 percent off sale on Steam changed everything.
It hit 156,000 players at once. More than double its old record.
Nearly four million people reportedly bought it during that one sale.
